headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 6 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Onto fresh climbing challenges! After Matthew Brennan’s second sprint success in Roquetes, the peloton of La Vuelta 26 face four categorised climbs, including the cat. 1 Puerto El Bartolo, from Alcossebre to Castello (177.5 km, 3,094m of elevation). The neutral start is set at 13:00, the start proper at 13:11 after a 5.2 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Memories from Alcossebre (and Castello)
subtext: Alcossebre is a stage town for the second time in La Vuelta history. In 2017, it hosted the finish of stage 5 after a route that is almost the same as today’s, on the opposite direction. The stage started in Benicassim, passed Castello at km 8, and then faced the ascents of the Alto del Desierto de las Palmas, Alto de Cabanes, Cool de la Bandereta and Puerto de La Serratella, also featured on today’s route. The breakaway made it to the finish and Alexey Lutsenko (now participating in La Vuelta 26 with NSN) took his first Grand Tour stage win.

headline: Lutsenko bids farewell: “Cycling has changed a lot”
subtext: Alexey Lutsenko (NSN Cycling Team) won a stage in Alcossebre (Ermita de Santa Lucía) in La Vuelta 17: “I remember! This was for me the first victory in a Grand Tour, I remember it very well. It was a hard stage, and also the last climb was a steep climb. It’s a nice memory for me. Now, cycling has changed a lot. It changed everything. For example, if 5-6 years ago your shape was as it’s best… now you would need to push double harder. But yes, I’m so happy because it’s my last year, my last Vuelta, and then I want to stop.” What will you do after? “This is a good question! I think, for me, maybe I need a couple of months to enjoy my family, and then I will see. Maybe I come back to cycling, maybe some project… I still live in Benidorm, but I go many times to Kazakhstan, and then I will move now to Moscow because my sister lives there. But, for example, now in summer is good to stay in Spain”

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 5.2 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) opened significant gaps as he achieved his biggest Grand Tour solo victory (50 km) in Andorra. Stage 5 to Roquetes didn’t change things. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is 2nd in the overall standings with a gap of 3’21’’. The next eight riders are within a minute of Roglic, from Enric Mas (Movistar) to Jay Vine (UAE Emirates XRG), 10th in the overall standings (+4’11’’).

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Leader of the points standings since his opening victory in Monaco, Tadej Pogacar is up to 82 points after his victory in Andorra. Since he wears La Roja, it will be Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease) racing with the green jersey. The British sprinter claimed 60 points with his two stage wins in Manosque and Roquetes. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) follows with 57 points.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: With Pavel Sivakov leading the bunch atop Puerto de Paüls, stage 5 brought no change in the first positions of the mountains standings. Tadej Pogacar is the leader with a tally of 23 points. Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) has 10 points and will wear the polka dot jersey today. Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) and Paul Double (Jayco AlUla) follow with 6 points each.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) retained the white jersey he had taken with his strong performance in Andorra. Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) trails by 21’’ and Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) by 59’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: UAE Emirates XRG still lead the team standings with a gap of 6’20’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike and 10’26’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) will once again race with a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider for the second time (stages 2 and 5).

headline: Stage 6 is ON!
subtext: The riders canbattle it out in the province of Castellon, home to a La Vuelta stage for the first time since 2023, when Kaden Groves won in Borriana.

headline: First attacks...
subtext: But the bunch is packed at km 3.

headline: Brenner hopes for "a nice birthday present"
subtext: Marco Brenner (Tudor) is hoping fora beautiful 24th birthday with a stage that could very well suit him: “The most important is to arrive safe and to have a nice birthday cake this afternoon [laughs]. I think it will be a super tricky day, especially with the gravel sector when we’ll be uphill, and then with the downhill to the finish. I think today we can maybe see the first breakaway. We will try with a few guys to take the breakaway, and then we see and hopefully take a good result and maybe make a nice birthday present for me.”

headline: Already past Alcala de Xivert
subtext: Alcala de Xivert (km 6) is Vicente Iturat’s hometown, winner of 4 La Vuelta stages and the points standings 1957. It was also the finish of stage 7 of La Vuelta 1977, an edition outrageously dominated by Freddy Maertens: the Belgian icon was the overall leader from start to finish, with 13 stage wins.

headline: 8 riders on the move
subtext: The battle for the breakaway goes on after 10 kilometres of hard racing.

headline: All together at km 12
subtext: Many riders announced they wanted to break away today. "If the breakaway takes a lot of time to form, then it becomes less of a workload for UAE to control the race and then go for the stage win", Jack Haig (Netcompany Ineos) warns. "But I imagine probably a strong breakaway will go for the win today."

headline: Lutsenko on the move with Bisiaux
subtext: Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) and Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) set off from the bunch at km 16 and are riding a few metres ahead of the peloton. Meanwhile, Jay Vine (UAE Emirates XRG) returns to the bunch after a mechanical.

headline: 15 seconds at km 18
subtext: Alexey Lutsenko and Léo Bisiaux keep pushing.

headline: 7 chasers behind Lustenko and Bisiaux
subtext: The gap from the lead duo to the bunch is still 15 seconds. And there are seven chasers in between.

headline: The chasers are caught by the bunch
subtext: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) still lead the way.

headline: 1 gap of 24'' at km 24
subtext: Lutsenko and Bisiaux pushed their lead up to 33'' but the battle goes on behind them.

headline: De la Cruz and Kron in pursuit
subtext: David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5) and Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) are chasing 25'' behind Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN). The gap to the bunch: 31''.

headline: De la Cruz and Kron are caught
subtext: The gap to the lead duo is down to 20''.

headline: De la Cruz aims for today's break on known terrain
subtext: David de la Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5): “Today is definitely a good day for a breakaway. I know the finish, though I’m not familiar with the new section of the Bartolo; but the Desierto de las Palmas is a climb I know quite well. I think it’s a perfect day for a breakaway and we’ll try as teams to be there because I reckon the win could go to the breakaway today.” "Puerto El Bartolo is going to be a tough climb because, as I say, the Desierto de las Palmas is a very well-known climb in the Castellon area – it’s lovely – and I’ve competed in the Spanish championships there, on a similar route. And although I’m not familiar with that final section, I’m sure it’s going to be incredibly tough and that’s where today’s stage will be decided."

headline: 30 kilometres of battle
subtext: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) are 20 seconds ahead of the bunch. Walter Calzoni (Pinarello Q36.5) sets off in pursuit.

headline: Calzoni joins Bisiaux and Lutsenko
subtext: The peloton are right behind the lead trio.

headline: The attackers are caught at km 33
subtext: They're at the bottom of the first categorised climb of the day, Puerto de la Serratella (14km at 3.8%).

headline: Attacks keep flying
subtext: Sixteen riders have just opened a small gap (km 36).

headline: Back together again
subtext: This is the most intense battle for the break so far at La Vuelta 26.

headline: 39.4 km in the first hour
subtext: The riders have already climbed 1,000 metres of elevation gain.

headline: Moniquet: "The battle lasts a bit longer than in the second or third week"
subtext: Breakaway specialist Sylvain Moniquet (Cofidis) described at the start thedynamics he expected in this first part of the stage: “At the start of the first week, it’s always a bit… Everyone’s still a bit fresh, so I think there are still plenty of riders who can try to get into the breakaways. The battle lasts a bit longer than in the second or third week, when a large part of the peloton is tired and drops out quite quickly on the first climbs, so it’s always a bit easier. The later on we get, the easier it is. Today I think it’s going to be a stage for the breakaway riders, unless UAE decide otherwise. The start is quite hilly, so there’s a chance the battle will go on for quite a while. The finish is also very tough, so I think we’ll see a strong group of climbers battling it out for victory at the finish.”

subtext: The attackers haven't managed to break away.

headline: Pogacar follows a group of chasers
subtext: Vermaerke and Vine are with the race leader. Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is also there, 40 seconds behind the leaders with 93 km remaining.

headline: Beloki has abandoned
subtext: Markel Beloki (EF Education-EasyPost) is the second rider out of La Vuelta 26 today, after Josh Tarling (Netcompany Ineos).

headline: The chasers are reeled in
subtext: The peloton are 30 seconds behind the leaders with 91 km to go.

headline: Debruyne is the main GC threat at the front
subtext: The young Belgian is 12th in the overall standings with a gap of 4'44''.

headline: UAE Emirates XRG drive the bunch
subtext: The attackers will soon enter the final 80 kilometres with a lead of 1'45''.

headline: Debruyne: "The breakaways are the best chance to get a good result"
subtext: Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) annoucned this morninghe wanted to make the break: “After the Tour, when I was healthy, we made a new plan, and then we decided to come to La Vuelta. First of all, I want to finish La Vuelta this time! Last year, I had to stop after stage 10 or 11 because of sickness, so this year for sure I want to finish it. For today, I want to start with a breakaway, and then we will see. And for the next days, I think the breakaways are the best chance to get a good result.”

headline: Heading for the main challenges of the day
subtext: The first challenges eventually saw 16 riders break away. Now they make their way to Benicassim, to face two ascents on the same slopes. The Alto del Desierto de las Palmas is an emblematic ascent in the are. It will be summited a first time with 48.9 km to go, after a 7.6 km ascent at 4.9%. Then, the peloton will return to Benicassim and tackle the ascent again. But they will continue climbing all the way to the Puerto El Bartolo. The final part of the ascent is the trickiest: it features a 1.9 km gravel section and gradients up to 20%. All in all, the ascent is 9.4 km long with an average gradient of 7.1% on irregular slopes.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Memories from Benicassim
subtext: Passed twice on today’s course (km 117 and 141.8), Benicassim first hosted La Vuelta stage in 1969 (stage 8), with Spain’s Ramon Saez taking the win ahead of the overall leader, Belgium’s Raymond Steegmans. Benicassim hosted the Gran Salida in 1990 with an ITT wonky Pello Ruiz Cabestany. Benicassim is also a classic venue for local events such as the Volta a la Comunitat Valencia.

headline: 2 minutes
subtext: The 16 attackers are 65 km from the finish. The peloton trail by 2'03''.

subtext: 14 stage wins - Wout van Aert (Tour de France x10, La Vuelta x3, Giro d'Italia x1) 3 - Pello Bilbao (Giro d'Italia x2, Tour de France x1) 2 - Santiago Buitrago (Giro d'Italia x2) 1 - Patrick Konrad (Tour de France x1) 1 - Urko Berrade (La Vuelta x1) 1 - Andreas Kron (La Vuelta x1)

headline: Van Aert takes 20 points at the intermediate sprint

subtext: The attackers face 7.6 km of climbing at 4.9%.

subtext: Bahrain Victorious rely on Santiago Buitrago in the breakaway. The gap is up to 2'40''.

headline: Diaz accelerates
subtext: The Spanish climber opens a gap into the last kilometre of ascent. The average speed after three hours: 42.3 km/h.

headline: Diaz and Buitrago battle for the points at the summit
subtext: There are 10 riders in the lead atop the Alto del Desierto de las Palmas: Craps, Gloag, Garofoli, Kron, Canal, Buitrago, Diaz, Albanese, Debruyne, Berrade. Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG) pulls the bunch with a gap of 2'35''.

headline: The gap has decreased on the downhill
subtext: The attackers return to the valley with a lead of 2'10''. The riders who were dropped on the ascent have returned to the front except for Van Aert.

headline: The situation stabilises on the valley
subtext: The leaders are 5 kilometres away from the final climb. The peloton trail by 2'00''.

headline: Kuss: "I train on gravel roads quite a bit"
subtext: Can Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) make the most of the tricky ascent up Puerto El Bartolo? “I like gravel roads", the climber said at the start. "I train on gravel roads quite a bit. It’s always nice. In the race, it just depends on how the sector is and everything, but I’m sure they did everything to make it proper for a bike race. Coming from the mountain bike, it definitely helps, but today is just uphill, it doesn’t change so much. You just have to keep a bit more traction on the rear wheel. I think today is quite a different stage, but when you have two stage wins already, everybody in the team gets motivation. For sure, we have some different cards to play today.”

headline: Onto the final climb of the day
subtext: The attackers begin the ascent up Puerto El Bartolo. The last gap to the peloton: 1'37''.

headline: Bilbao is dropped from the lead group
subtext: The Spaniard pulled to try and give Buitrago a shot at the stage win today. The gap is down to 1'25''.

headline: Craps and Kron up the ante
subtext: Buitrago chases them down 7 km from the summit. The breakaway explodes.

headline: Vine sets the pace in the peloton
subtext: The Australian climber is followed by Pablo Torres and then Tadej Pogacar. The gap keeps decreasing: 1'10'' with 27 km to go.

headline: The most beautiful sport in the world
5 kilometres to the summit; Widar in trouble
subtext: Seven riders remain at the front: Buitrago, Debruyne, Garofoli, Kron, Diaz, Craps, Berrade. The gap to the bunch is down to 58''. Jay Vine is spent. Pablo Torres now sets the pace. And Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) is dropped! There are around 30 riders.

headline: Debruyne and Pogacar increase the pace
subtext: The gap is down to 30 seconds with 4 km left of climbing.

headline: Pogacar has dropped everyone
subtext: Onley was the last rival on his wheel. He is 20 seconds behind Debruyne, who has gone solo with 3.5 km left on the climb.

headline: Onto the gravel section
subtext: Debruyne is alone at the front.

headline: Pogacar catches and drops Debruyne
subtext: They are just inside the last 3 kilometres of ascent.

headline: Mas catches Debruyne
subtext: The Spaniard has distanced a small group led by Roglic. Gall is on the Slovenian's wheel. Carapaz and Onley struggle to keep up.

headline: 1 kilometre to the summit for Pogacar
subtext: Mas is the closest chaser, around 15 seconds behind the Slovenian.

headline: Mas catches Pogacar
subtext: They're at the summit. The Spaniard goes first.

headline: Mas sets the pace on the downhill
subtext: Roglic, Gall and Debruyne went over the top with a gap of 30''.

headline: Pogacar goes off road
subtext: Quite the scare for the Slovenian, but he rapidly gets back to Mas' wheel!

subtext: Can the Spaniard get the better of the Slovenian star?

headline: Tadej Pogacar wins stage 6 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: Already his third stage win in this edition!
